units.text: Before running any CLI command, read the matched skill's SKILL.md; never guess command syntax or supported flags.
units.note: Lite: exact syntax lives only in references/commands/<top>.md cards; read the card before running `ocl <command>`.

units.text: Report a CLI command (and its result) only after it actually ran; never claim a command ran or fabricate its output.
Use CLI output for live data (prices, balances, holdings, signals); never answer live data from skill text or model memory.
Do not use the retired `onchainos preflight` command.
units.note: Lite has no preflight/installer; `ocl doctor` covers environment/egress/login diagnostics.

units.text: Installation, update, and reinstall use `npx -y @okxweb3/onchainos-installer install` (add `--beta` when needed).
units.note: Lite skill folder is self-contained; no installer or upgrade path.

units.text: For token research, market overview, smart-money, new-token scanning, wallet analysis, portfolio, or wallet monitoring requests, read `workflows/INDEX.md` first (before individual skills).
For Chinese-language requests also read `workflows/references/keyword-glossary.md` (Chinese slang → workflow mapping).
Wallet actions and security checks → `okx-agentic-wallet` skill.
units.note: Covers wallet, security, swap/bridge execution, portfolio etc. in upstream; lite merges skills.

units.text: Named third-party DApps → `okx-dapp-discovery` skill.
Agent identity, task lifecycle, marketplace subscriptions, and task monitoring → `okx-ai` skill.
HTTP 402, x402, MPP, and payment IDs → `okx-agent-payments-protocol` skill.
DeFi yield, protocol positions, deposits, withdrawals, and rewards → `okx-defi` skill.
OnchainOS installation, onboarding, OKX.AI introduction, and support → `okx-guide` skill.
units.note: The "installation" part is obsolete in lite; onboarding/introduction/support routing still applies.

units.text: If a request can plausibly match more than one skill, read every candidate SKILL.md and apply their routing rules; the skills own capability lists, aliases, command indexes, and tie-breakers.
Authoring rule: the top-level routing doc must not duplicate skills' capability lists, aliases, command indexes, or tie-breakers.

units.text: If the user's query contains Chinese text, read `references/keyword-glossary.md` for trigger mappings (stated in INDEX.md and repeated in every workflow doc's "## Keyword Glossary" section).
Token Research workflow (`token-research.md`) triggers: "analyze token", "research [address]", "is this token safe"; additional triggers in the workflow doc: "what is this token", "token deep dive".
Daily Brief workflow (`daily-brief.md`) triggers: "daily brief", "morning brief", "market overview"; additional triggers in the workflow doc: "what's the market doing today".

Smart Money Signals workflow (`smart-money-signals.md`) triggers: "smart money", "what are whales buying", "copy trading signals"; additional triggers in the workflow doc: "what is smart money buying", "KOL buys".

New Token Screening workflow (`new-token-screening.md`) triggers: "scan new tokens", "pump.fun tokens", "meme token scan"; additional triggers in the workflow doc: "new token screening", "what's new on pump.fun".

Wallet Analysis workflow (`wallet-analysis.md`) triggers: "analyze wallet", "check this address", "is this wallet worth following"; additional triggers in the workflow doc: "what's this wallet's trading style".
Portfolio Check workflow (`portfolio-check.md`) triggers: "portfolio", "check my holdings", "my wallet"; additional triggers in the workflow doc: "what tokens do I have", "my assets".
Wallet Monitor workflow (`wallet-monitor.md`) triggers: "watch wallet", "monitor this wallet", "watch [address]"; additional triggers in the workflow doc: "alert me when this wallet trades".

Wallet Monitor (WS) workflow (`wallet-monitor-ws.md`) triggers: "background monitor", "offline monitor", "WebSocket monitor"; additional triggers in the workflow doc: "monitor in background", "long-running wallet watch".
If no workflow matches, fall back to individual skills.

Workflow doc sections, in order: `# {Name}`, `> {one-liner}`, `## Triggers`, `## Required Skills`, `## Input`, `## Steps` (each `### Step N — {name} [required | recommended] (parallel | sequential | conditional: {condition})`), `## Output Template`, `## Actions`, optional `## Follow-up Workflows`.
units.note: Actual workflow docs additionally carry `## Keyword Glossary` and `## CLI` (composite command or "agent-orchestrated") sections not listed in the template.

units.text: Every step is labeled `[required]` or `[recommended]` and `(parallel)` / `(sequential)` / `(conditional: <condition>)`: required steps must run, recommended steps are optional enrichment, parallel steps' commands may run concurrently, conditional steps run only when the condition holds.
Token budget: a single workflow doc must be ≤ 1.5K tokens.
CLI-first: workflows use only `onchainos` CLI commands — never reference MCP tool names.
units.note: Lite: `ocl <command>`.

units.text: Workflow docs are English only — no inline Chinese; add a `## Keyword Glossary` section pointing to `references/keyword-glossary.md` instead.
Workflows follow the token risk controls defined in `okx-agentic-wallet` SKILL.md — do not redefine them in workflow docs.
Script mode: use `--format` only when the command documents it; otherwise consume the command's machine-readable (JSON) output directly.
`## Follow-up Workflows` is optional — add it only when multiple downstream workflows are explicitly chained; `## Actions` is sufficient for most workflows.
Users may use Chinese crypto slang or platform-specific terms; map them to the matching workflow via the glossary table.
Chinese "帮我看看这个币 / 这个币怎么样 / 查一下这个代币 / 这个币安全吗" = analyze token, research token, is this token safe → Token Research.
Chinese "今天市场怎么样 / 每日简报 / 市场概况" = daily brief, morning brief, market overview → Daily Brief.
Chinese "聪明钱在买什么 / 跟单信号 / KOL在买什么 / 聪明钱信号" = smart money, copy trading signals, what are whales buying → Smart Money Signals.
Chinese "帮我扫新币 / 打狗 / 扫链 / pump.fun有什么 / 有什么新币 / memepump新币" = scan new tokens, new token screening, pump.fun tokens → New Token Screening.
Chinese "分析这个钱包 / 这个地址怎么样 / 这个钱包值得跟吗 / 这个地址什么风格" = analyze wallet, check this address, is this wallet worth following → Wallet Analysis.
Chinese "看看我的持仓 / 我的钱包 / 我有什么币 / 我的资产" = portfolio, check my holdings, my wallet (also row: 看看我的持仓 → check my portfolio) → Portfolio Check.
units.note: Glossary lists 看看我的持仓 twice (portfolio / check my portfolio), both → Portfolio Check.

units.text: Chinese "帮我盯着这个钱包 / 监控地址 / 盯着 [address]" = watch wallet, monitor this wallet → Wallet Monitor.
Chinese "后台监控 / 挂ws盯着 / 离线监控 / 挂一个ws盯着 / 长期盯着这个钱包" = background monitor, offline monitor, WebSocket monitor → Wallet Monitor (WS).
Chinese "看聚类列表 / 看同车钱包" = show cluster list, show co-invested wallets → Token Research → Step 2 (cluster data).
Chinese "查 dev 其他项目 / dev 跑路记录" = show dev projects, dev rug history → Token Research → Step 3 (launchpad/dev data).
Chinese "停止监控" = stop monitoring → Wallet Monitor (exit the poll loop).
Chinese "盯着这个币" = watch this token → Wallet Monitor.
Chinese "看看 [symbol]" = research [symbol] → Token Research.
Daily Brief combines market pulse, smart money activity, new token launches, and portfolio alerts into one morning report. Required skills: okx-dex-market, okx-agentic-wallet.
Daily Brief inputs: `chain` (optional, default Solana); `wallet_address` (optional — enables Step 4 portfolio alerts).
Daily Brief has no single CLI composite — it is agent-orchestrated: the agent runs the atomic commands of four cross-skill steps directly and summarises their outputs in prose.
units.note: No `workflow daily-brief` subcommand exists in 4.6.3.

units.text: Step 1 — Market pulse [required] (parallel): `market prices --tokens "<chainIndex>:<SOL_addr>,<chainIndex>:<BTC_addr>,<chainIndex>:<ETH_addr>"`; `token hot-tokens --chain <chain>`; `market kline --address <SOL_addr> --chain solana --bar 1D --limit 7` (7 daily candles = SOL 7-day trend).
`market prices` requires `--tokens` in `chainIndex:address` format (comma-separated pairs).
`token hot-tokens` returns up to 100 results — display only the top 10.
Daily Brief Step 1 presents: SOL / BTC / ETH prices, SOL 7-day trend, top 10 trending tokens.
Step 2 — Smart money activity [recommended] (parallel): `signal list --chain <chain>`; `tracker activities --tracker-type smart_money --chain <chain>`.

units.source: workflows/daily-brief.md#Step 2 — Smart money activity; workflows/wallet-monitor.md#Step 2 — Poll loop
units.text: `tracker activities` requires `--tracker-type` (workflows use `smart_money` for smart-money feed and `multi_address` with `--wallet-address` for specific wallets).
Daily Brief Step 2 presents: SM signal tokens grouped by wallet count; recent SM/KOL buys and sells.
Step 3 — New token activity [recommended] (sequential): `memepump tokens --chain <chain> --stage MIGRATED`.

units.source: workflows/daily-brief.md#Step 3 — New token activity; workflows/new-token-screening.md#Step 1 — Fetch
units.text: `memepump tokens` has no `--limit` param. `--stage MIGRATED` returns tokens within 72h of migration; `MIGRATING` returns tokens within 24h of creation; tokens outside these windows are not returned.
Daily Brief Step 3: display top 10 recently migrated tokens with holder count, volume, SM count.

Step 4 — Portfolio alerts [recommended] (conditional: wallet_address provided): `portfolio all-balances --address <wallet> --chains <chain>`; `market portfolio-overview --address <wallet> --chain <chain>`.
Daily Brief Step 4 presents: holdings summary, overall PnL, notable 24h changes in held tokens.

Daily Brief output template: "DAILY BRIEF — {chain} — {date}"; MARKET: "BTC ${x} | ETH ${x} | SOL ${x}", "SOL 7D: {trend summary}"; HOT TOKENS table (#, Symbol, Price, 24h%, Vol); SMART MONEY: "Buying: {sym} ({n} wallets)...", "Selling: {sym} ({n} wallets)...", "Notable: {addr} bought ${x} of {sym}"; NEW TOKENS table (Token, MCap, Holders, SM); [if wallet provided] PORTFOLIO: "Total: ${x} | PnL(24h): ${x}", "Moves: {sym} {+/-x}%, ...".
Daily Brief follow-ups: "research [symbol]" → Token Research; "what is smart money buying" → Smart Money Signals.
New Token Screening scans Launchpad new tokens, enriches top results with safety and dev data, and surfaces actionable candidates. Required skills: okx-dex-market, okx-agentic-wallet.

New Token Screening inputs (all optional): chain (default Solana), protocol (default All), min_holders, min_bonding_percent, top10_hold_percent_max (default: CLI default). Filter params pass through to `memepump tokens`; users may override via natural language (e.g. "only show tokens with 100+ holders").
units.note: Flag mapping in 4.6.3: min_holders→--min-holders, min_bonding_percent→--min-bonding-percent, top10_hold_percent_max→--max-top10-holdings-percent, protocol→--protocol-id-list. The `workflow new-tokens` composite accepts only --chain/--stage, so filters require the atomic `memepump tokens` path.

units.text: Complete New Token Screening in one command: `workflow new-tokens [--chain <chain>] [--stage MIGRATED|MIGRATING]` (defaults: solana, MIGRATED).
Step 1 — Fetch [required] (sequential): `memepump tokens --chain <chain> --stage MIGRATED`.
Users may filter `memepump tokens` with `--min-holders`, `--min-market-cap`, `--max-top10-holdings-percent`.
New Token Screening Step 1 presents a token list: name, symbol, mcap, holders, volume, SM count, creation time.

Step 2 — Safety + dev enrichment [recommended] (parallel per token, top 10): `security token-scan --tokens "<chainIndex>:<addr>"`; `token advanced-info --address <addr> --chain <chain>`; `memepump token-dev-info --address <addr> --chain <chain>`; `memepump token-bundle-info --address <addr> --chain <chain>`.
New Token Screening Step 2 presents per token: honeypot, tax flags, mint/freeze, dev rug count, dev holding %, bundle rate.

New Token Screening output template: "NEW TOKENS — {chain} — {timestamp}"; per token "#N {name} ({symbol})" then "MCap: ${x} | Holders: {n} | SM: {n} | Age: {n}h", "Honeypot: {Y/N} | Tax: {x}/{x}% | Mint: {A/R} | Freeze: {A/R}", "Dev Rugs: {n} | Dev Holding: {x}% | Bundle: {x}%".
New Token Screening follow-ups: "research [symbol]" → Token Research; "show dev projects for [symbol]" → show dev project history.
Portfolio Check shows wallet token balances, total value, and per-token PnL. Required skills: okx-agentic-wallet, okx-dex-market.
Portfolio Check inputs: `wallet_address` (required); `chain` (optional, default all supported chains).
units.note: Upstream does not say how to obtain the address for "my wallet"; lite can resolve it from the logged-in wallet (social-login flow → wallet addresses) or ask the user. Composite default chains when omitted: "1,501".

units.text: `workflow portfolio --address <addr> [--chains <chains>]` covers Step 1 (overview) only; Step 2 (per-token detail) is optional and agent-orchestrated — loop the atomic commands over each holding from Step 1.

Step 1 — Overview [required] (parallel): `portfolio all-balances --address <wallet> --chains <chain>`; `portfolio total-value --address <wallet> --chains <chain>`; `market portfolio-overview --address <wallet> --chain <chain>`.
`portfolio all-balances` and `portfolio total-value` use `--chains` (plural), unlike `market portfolio-overview --chain`.
Portfolio Check Step 1 presents: total value, token balances, PnL, win rate.

Step 2 — Per-token detail [recommended] (parallel per holding, agent-orchestrated): `market portfolio-token-pnl --address <wallet> --chain <chain> --token <addr>`; `token price-info --address <addr> --chain <chain>`. Not covered by `workflow portfolio` — run per holding only when a deeper per-token view is requested.
`market portfolio-token-pnl` uses `--token` (not `--token-address`).
Portfolio Check Step 2 presents per token: price, 24h change, realized / unrealized PnL, avg cost.

Portfolio Check output template: "PORTFOLIO — {short_addr}", "Total: ${x} | PnL(30d): ${x} | Win Rate: {x}%", "--- HOLDINGS ---", per holding "#N {sym} Balance: {n} | Value: ${x} | 24h: {x}% | PnL: ${x} | AvgCost: ${x}".
Portfolio Check follow-up: "research [symbol]" → Token Research.
Smart Money Signals collects smart money buy signals, aggregates by token, then runs due diligence on each signal token. Required skills: okx-dex-market, okx-agentic-wallet.
Smart Money Signals input: `chain` (optional, default Solana).
Complete Smart Money Signals in one command: `workflow smart-money [--chain <chain>]`.
Step 1 — Collect signals [required] (sequential): `signal list --chain <chain>`; aggregate by token — count distinct SM wallet addresses per token, sort descending by wallet count, take top 5.
Smart Money Signals Step 1 presents: token list with SM wallet count per token.

Step 2 — Per-token due diligence [required] (parallel per token, max 5): `token price-info --address <token> --chain <chain>`; `token advanced-info --address <token> --chain <chain>`; `security token-scan --tokens "<chainIndex>:<token>"`.

If `advanced-info.protocolId` is non-empty (launchpad token), also run in parallel: `memepump token-dev-info --address <token> --chain <chain>`; `memepump token-bundle-info --address <token> --chain <chain>`.
units.note: CLI rule (is_launchpad_token): protocolId must be a non-empty JSON string.

units.text: Smart Money Signals Step 2 presents per token: price, mcap, mint/freeze, honeypot, tax flags, dev rug history, bundle rate.

Smart Money Signals output template: "SMART MONEY SIGNALS — {chain} — {timestamp}", "Scanned: {n} signal tokens → Top {m} by SM wallet count"; per token "#N {name} ({symbol})", "SM Wallets: {n} | Price: ${x} | MCap: ${x}", "Honeypot: {Y/N} | Tax: {x}/{x}% | Mint: {A/R} | Freeze: {A/R}", [if protocolId non-empty] "Dev Rugs: {n} | Dev Holding: {x}% | Bundle: {x}%".
Smart Money Signals follow-up: "research [symbol]" → Token Research.
Token Research pulls price, contract, security, holders, top traders, and smart money signals for any token in one flow. Required skills: okx-dex-market, okx-agentic-wallet.
Token Research inputs: `token_address` or `query` (symbol/name) — one of them is required; `chain` optional (auto-detect).
Run Token Research with a contract address: `workflow token-research --address <addr> [--chain <chain>]`.

Step 0 — Token resolution (conditional: user gave a symbol/name, not an address): `workflow token-research --query <symbol> [--chain <chain>]` returns up to 5 search results (index, symbol, name, address, chain, price, market cap). Present them as a numbered list, let the user pick one, then re-invoke with `--address` of the selected token and continue from Step 1. Do not auto-pick.
units.note: CLI output step="select-token" with fixed message "Multiple tokens found. Please select one by number (1-5) to continue the full research workflow." even for a single result.

units.text: Step 1 — Core data [required] (parallel): prefer the composite `token report --address <addr> --chain <chain>` when available.
Step 1 fallback — run all 4 in parallel: `token info`, `token price-info`, `token advanced-info` (each `--address <addr> --chain <chain>`), and `security token-scan --tokens "<chainIndex>:<addr>"`.
Token liquidity comes from `price-info.liquidity`.
`security token-scan` returns boolean risk flags only; combine with `advanced-info.tokenTags` for tax info.
Token Research Step 1 presents: name, symbol, age (from `advanced-info.createTime`), price, mcap, 24h vol, 24h change, honeypot, buy/sell tax flags, mint/freeze authority, liquidity, LP burned %.

Step 2 — On-chain structure [recommended] (parallel): `token holders --address <addr> --chain <chain>`; `token cluster-overview --address <addr> --chain <chain>`; `token top-trader --address <addr> --chain <chain>`; `signal list --chain <chain> --token-address <addr>`.
`token holders` defaults to 20 results; pass `--limit 100` for the top 100.
`token cluster-overview` may return HTTP 500 for brand-new tokens — skip it gracefully (omit cluster data) if unavailable.

Token Research Step 2 presents: holder count, Top 10 holding %, tag distribution (SM / Whale / Insider), linked cluster groups + supply %, top trader PnL breakdown (profitable / losing / holding / exited), SM signal wallet count.

Step 3 — Launchpad supplement [recommended] (conditional: `contract.protocolId` from Step 1 is non-empty): `memepump token-details`, `memepump token-dev-info`, `memepump token-bundle-info`, `memepump similar-tokens` (each `--address <addr> --chain <chain>`). Skip entirely when `protocolId` is empty (token is not from a launchpad).
units.note: `contract` = advanced-info block (composite output core.contract); same field as advanced-info.protocolId in Smart Money Signals.

units.text: Token Research Step 3 presents: bonding curve progress, dev tokens created, dev rug count, dev holding %, bundle rate, dev's other projects.

Token Research output template: "TOKEN: {symbol} ({chain})", "Address: {addr} | Age: {n}d"; --- PRICE & MARKET --- "Price | MCap | 24h Vol", "1h: {x}% | 4h: {x}% | 24h: {x}%"; --- SECURITY --- "Honeypot: {Y/N} | Buy Tax: {x}% | Sell Tax: {x}%", "Mint: {Active/Revoked} | Freeze: {Active/Revoked}", "Risk Level: {1-5} | Tags: {list}"; --- LIQUIDITY --- "Total Pool Value: ${x} | LP Burned: {x}%"; --- HOLDERS --- "Total: {n} | Top10: {x}%", "SM: {n} Whales: {n} Insiders: {n}", "Linked Groups: {n} ({x}% of supply)"; --- TOP TRADERS (by PnL) --- "Total | Profitable | Losing", "Still Holding | Fully Exited", "Avg PnL | Best: +{x}% | Worst: {x}%"; --- SMART MONEY --- "SM Buy Signals (24h): {n} wallets"; [if protocolId non-empty] --- DEV / LAUNCHPAD --- "Dev Rug History: {n} | Dev Holding: {x}%", "Bundle: {x}% | Dev Other Projects: {n} (Survival: {x}%)".
Token Research follow-ups: "show cluster list" / "show co-invested wallets" → show cluster details; "show dev projects" → show dev project history; "watch this token" → Wallet Monitor.
Wallet Analysis pulls a wallet's performance metrics, trading behavior, current holdings, and recent activity. Required skills: okx-dex-market, okx-agentic-wallet.
Wallet Analysis inputs: `wallet_address` (required); `chain` (optional, auto-detect).
units.note: Composite `workflow wallet-analysis` defaults chain to solana.

units.text: Complete Wallet Analysis in one command: `workflow wallet-analysis --address <addr> [--chain <chain>]`.

Step 1 — Performance [required] (parallel): `market portfolio-overview --address <wallet> --chain <chain> --time-frame 3` (7d); same with `--time-frame 4` (30d/1M); `portfolio all-balances --address <wallet> --chains <chain>`.
`market portfolio-overview --time-frame` values: 1=1D, 2=3D, 3=7D, 4=1M, 5=3M.
Wallet Analysis Step 1 presents: 7d vs 30d PnL, win rate, realized profit, trade count, current holdings.
Step 2 — Trading behavior [recommended] (sequential): `market portfolio-recent-pnl --address <wallet> --chain <chain>`; present per-token PnL and trading frequency.

Step 3 — Recent activity [recommended] (sequential): `tracker activities --tracker-type multi_address --wallet-address <wallet> --chain <chain>`; present most recent trades — time, token, direction, amount.

Wallet Analysis output template: "WALLET: {short_addr} ({chain})"; PERFORMANCE table with 7d / 30d columns for PnL, Win Rate, Realized, Trades; HOLDINGS table (Token, Balance, Value, Unrealized); BEHAVIOR "Avg Hold: {duration} | Avg Size: ${x} | Freq: {n}/day", "Most Traded: {sym1}, {sym2}, {sym3}"; TOKEN PnL table (Token, Realized, Unrealized); RECENT table (Time, Token, Action, Amount).
Wallet Analysis follow-ups: "watch [address]" → Wallet Monitor; "research [token_they_hold]" → Token Research.
Wallet Monitor continuously polls wallet activity in-session and alerts on new trades — it does NOT execute trades.
Wallet Monitor inputs: `wallet_addresses` (required, max 10); `chain` (optional, auto); `polling_interval` (optional, default 60s). Required skills: okx-dex-market, okx-agentic-wallet.
units.note: Workflow caps at 10 addresses although `tracker activities --wallet-address` accepts max 20.

units.text: Wallet Monitor has no CLI composite — it is an agent-orchestrated polling loop with conditional per-event enrichment and stateful diffing across ticks. For a background session use the WebSocket variant (`wallet-monitor-ws.md`).
Step 1 — Setup [required] (sequential): confirm the monitoring address list and polling interval with the user before starting.
Step 2 — Poll loop [required] (sequential, repeating every `interval` seconds): `tracker activities --tracker-type multi_address --wallet-address <wallet> --chain <chain>`.
`tracker activities --wallet-address` takes multiple addresses comma-separated, max 20; `--tracker-type` is required.

Diff each poll against the previous one to detect new transactions. On a new buy, enrich the bought token: `token price-info --address <new_token> --chain <chain>`; `security token-scan --tokens "<chainIndex>:<new_token>"`.

Wallet Monitor alert format: "[{time}] ALERT — {label/addr}", "{Buy/Sell} {symbol} — ${amount}", "Price: ${x} | MCap: ${x}", "Honeypot: {Y/N} | Tax: {x}/{x}%", "→ \"research [symbol]\" | → \"buy [amount] [native_token] of [symbol]\"".
Multi-wallet convergence alert: "[MULTI-WALLET] {n} wallets bought {symbol}".
Exit the poll loop when the user says "stop monitoring".

Wallet Monitor follow-ups: "research [symbol]" → Token Research; "stop monitoring" exits the loop; alerts suggest "buy [amount] [native_token] of [symbol]" as a user-initiated follow-up (routes to swap; the monitor never trades itself).
Wallet Monitor (WS) configures and starts a background WebSocket monitoring session that runs independently of the conversation. Required skills: okx-dex-market, okx-agentic-wallet.
Wallet Monitor (WS) inputs: `wallet_addresses` (required, max 10); `chain` (optional, auto).
units.note: Workflow caps at 10 while `ws start --wallet-addresses` accepts max 200.

units.text: Polling vs WebSocket: runs in — AI in-session loop vs background WS session; AI presence — required vs not needed after setup; latency — polling_interval (default 60s) vs real-time push; token cost — each poll round vs setup + on-demand poll only; best for — online real-time discussion vs background / offline / scripting.
units.note: CLI fact: `ws start --idle-timeout` defaults to 30m — the session auto-stops if not polled within that window (0 disables), which limits "offline" use unless set.

units.text: Step 1 — Check available channels [required] (sequential): `ws channels`; `ws channel-info --channel address-tracker-activity`. Present available channels and the subscription parameters for address-tracker-activity.
The channel name passed to `ws start` must match what `ws channel-info` returns (wallet monitoring uses `address-tracker-activity`).

Step 2 — Start session [required] (sequential): `ws start --channel address-tracker-activity --wallet-addresses "<addr1>,<addr2>" --chain-index <chainIndex>`. Present the session ID and subscription confirmation.
`ws start --wallet-addresses` takes comma-separated values (max 200); `--chain-index` accepts comma-separated chain indexes (e.g. `501` Solana, `1` Ethereum). Do not use `--params` JSON.
Step 3 — Verify session [required] (sequential): `ws list`; confirm the new session is in the active sessions list.
Step 4 — Show consumption options [required]: manual poll `ws poll --id <session_id>`; scripted poll example `while true; do onchainos ws poll --id <session_id> --limit 50; sleep 30; done`.

When the user runs `ws poll` and new events are returned, optionally enrich each event token: `token price-info --address <event_token> --chain <chain>`; `security token-scan --tokens "<chainIndex>:<event_token>"`.

Wallet Monitor (WS) output template: "WS MONITOR STARTED", "Session: {session_id}", "Channel: address-tracker-activity", "Addresses: {addr1}, {addr2}...", "Status: Active", then how-to lines: check events `onchainos ws poll --id {session_id}`; stop `onchainos ws stop --id {session_id}`; list all sessions `onchainos ws list`.
units.note: Lite: render these hints as `ocl ws ...`.

units.text: Wallet Monitor (WS) follow-ups: "research [symbol]" for tokens seen in poll events → Token Research; "stop monitoring" → `ws stop --id <session_id>`.
Every workflow calls `security token-scan` with `--tokens "<chainIndex>:<addr>"` (chainIndex:address pair), not `--address`.
